memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the serpent was more crafty than any of the wild animals the Lord God had made. He said to the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?" — Gen 3:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Have you noticed that the very first attack on humanity was not big and loud? It came quietly, as a small question. The serpent did not deny God outright. He simply asked, "Did God really say...?" — and with those few words, he planted a seed of doubt in the woman's heart.

See how cleverly he twisted things. God had given Adam and Eve freedom to enjoy every tree except one (Gen 2:16–17). But the serpent made it sound as though God was holding them back from everything. This is often how temptation still works today. It rarely begins by telling us to reject God. It begins by making us wonder whether His Word can truly be trusted, and whether His commands are really for our good.

Dear friend, the enemy has not changed his method. He still whispers, "Did God really say?" whenever we face a choice. But we are not left defenceless. When Jesus met the same tempter in the wilderness, He did not argue — He simply stood on what was written (Matt 4:4). The second Adam held firm where the first one fell.

When doubt comes knocking, we do not need clever answers. We only need to rest on what God has clearly said, trusting that the God who loves us cannot lie to us (Jn 8:44).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. In which areas of your life do you find it hardest to believe that God's commands are truly for your good?
2. When doubt whispers "Did God really say?", where do you usually turn first?
3. How might knowing Scripture better help you stand firm the next time temptation comes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your Word is true and every command flows from Your love for me. When the enemy tempts me to doubt You, help me to stand firmly on what You have said, just as Jesus did. Amen.
